title: U.S. House · Michigan's 3rd District
area: Michigan's 3rd Congressional District — Grand Rapids and central-western Michigan.

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 3rd District D+4 for the 2026 cycle. Kamala Harris won the district 53.1%–45.2% in 2024.
Incumbent Hillary Scholten was unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. Terri DeBoer defeated Ryan Cushman in the Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote.

candidates.name: Hillary Scholten
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Scholten is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 3rd District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress she was an immigration attorney, including work at the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center and the U.S. Department of Justice's Board of Immigration Appeals.

background.text: Born in Michigan in 1982; earned a bachelor's degree from Gordon College (2002) and a J.D. from the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law (2012).

Worked as senior counsel at Miller Johnson, as a staff attorney with the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center, and as a judicial law clerk and attorney advisor with the U.S. Department of Justice Board of Immigration Appeals.

priorities.text: Leads the Lowering Costs Caucus and has pushed the administration to address rising energy prices, citing tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as factors straining household budgets.

Says Congress must overhaul the immigration system, citing her background as an immigration attorney, and cosponsored the bipartisan Dignity Act to combine border security with a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants already in the country.
priorities.quote: Congress must act now to reform our immigration system. It's time to allow hardworking families to move out of the shadows and into the full light of the American dream.

priorities.text: Says everyone deserves access to high-quality reproductive health care and has hosted local roundtables on the issue.
priorities.quote: Everyone deserves access to the high-quality reproductive care they need.

positions.summary: A member of the Pro-Choice Caucus, says abortion rights need to be federally codified and criticized a Supreme Court decision for leaving emergency abortion access unresolved.
positions.quote: For the first time ever, women today have less rights than our mothers and grandmothers. ... We must federally codify the right to reproductive care and save lives while we have the chance.

positions.summary: Says gun safety laws that keep firearms out of the hands of abusers are needed to protect women, in a statement on a bill addressing violence against women.
positions.quote: what we really need to move the needle on protecting women are gun safety laws to keep firearms out of abusers' hands

positions.summary: Cosponsored the bipartisan Dignity Act, which pairs border security and infrastructure funding with a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants already living in the U.S. and new legal pathways for asylum seekers and economic migrants.
positions.quote: This historic bipartisan legislation would address border security and infrastructure challenges, tackle critical workforce development issues, create legal status for undocumented immigrants already living in the United States, establish new pathways for asylum seekers, and create new legal pathways for economic migrants and unaccompanied minors.

positions.summary: Says she defends the Affordable Care Act and works to expand it, along with capping prescription drug and insulin costs.
positions.quote: I vote to cap the cost of critical prescription drugs and insulin, and I defend the Affordable Care Act and work every day to expand on it.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Small Business (Contracting and Infrastructure; Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains) and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Water Resources and Environment).
Cosponsored the Dignity Act of 2025, bipartisan immigration legislation addressing border security, a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants, and new legal immigration pathways.

candidates.name: Terri DeBoer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 78.6% of the vote

summary.text: DeBoer is a longtime Grand Rapids television meteorologist running as the Republican nominee against incumbent Hillary Scholten.

background.text: Born in Fort Dix, New Jersey; earned a high school diploma from C.M. Russell High School.
Worked as a meteorologist at WWMT-TV, WOOD-TV, and FOX-17, and was inducted into the Michigan Emmy Silver Circle.
Has served as a board member for the Mental Health Foundation of West Michigan and the Grand Rapids Griffins Youth Foundation, and on the Millennium Park Commission.
